title: The exposome in respiratory diseases: multiple preventable risk factors from early life to adulthood.
ehr_evidence: The three reviewed studies used prospective cohorts rather than EHR data: the INMA Spanish birth cohort (urine phthalate metabolites and repeated spirometry), the RHINESSA cohort (questionnaire-based diagnoses and land-use-regression air pollution/NDVI exposure modeling), and the web-based NutriNet-Santé cohort (self-reported questionnaires and GIS-based residential exposures).
summary: This journal club commentary reviews three cohort studies (INMA, RHINESSA, NutriNet-Santé) investigating environmental exposures (gestational phthalates, air pollution, greenness, and a multi-domain exposome) and their associations with respiratory outcomes (childhood lung function, asthma, rhinitis, and impaired lung function).
key_findings: INMA: gestational phthalate metabolite mixture associated with lower childhood FVC and FEV1, especially in early childhood; FEV1 z-score coefficient at age 4 was -0.024 (95% CI -0.041 to -0.008) per 10% increase in MiBP and -0.018 (95% CI -0.032 to -0.004) per 10% increase in MBzP, with most individual associations not statistically significant; WQS regression identified MBzP as an important contributor to the mixture effect.

RHINESSA: air pollutants associated with increased risk of asthma attack for the 'year before the study' window (adjusted OR 1.60-2.46); NO2, O3 and PM10 associated for other windows (adjusted OR 1.29-2.25); air pollutants except O3 associated with rhinitis only for the year-before window (adjusted OR 1.25-1.50); PM2.5 and O3 during childhood/adolescence associated with FEV1/FVC <LLN (adjusted OR 2.65-5.95); greenness (NDVI) not associated with asthma or rhinitis but associated with FEV1/FVC <LLN (adjusted OR 1.68 and 1.53).

NutriNet-Santé: three early-life and one lifestyle exposure profiles associated with more asthma symptoms (mean score ratio 1.11-1.96) and uncontrolled asthma (OR 1.45-2.88), with dose-response findings for all early-life profiles.
captured_features: Nine gestational phthalate metabolites in maternal urine (MEP, MiBP, MnBP, MCMHP, MBzP, MEHHP, MEOHP, MECPP, MEHP)
Repeated spirometry: FVC, FEV1, FEV1/FVC z-scores at ages 4, 7, 9 and 11 years
Air pollution exposures: NO2, PM10, PM2.5, black carbon, O3 via land-use regression
Greenness estimated by NDVI from satellite measurements at 300 m buffer
Questionnaire-defined physician-diagnosed asthma, asthma attack, current rhinitis
Impaired lung function below lower limit of normal (z-score <1.64)
87 exposome variables across socioeconomic, external environment, early-life environment and lifestyle-anthropometric domains
Asthma symptom score (0-5) and asthma control categories
study_design: Journal club commentary reviewing three cohort studies (INMA prospective birth cohort, RHINESSA retrospective cohort with matched case-control, and NutriNet-Santé cross-sectional analysis from a web-based cohort)
population: INMA: 641 mother-child pairs from Spain; RHINESSA: 3428 adults from Norway and Sweden (mean age 28 years); NutriNet-Santé: 20,833 adults from France (mean age 56.2 years, 72% women)
exposure_domain: Environmental exposome: gestational phthalate exposure, air pollution (NO2, PM10, PM2.5, black carbon, O3), greenness (NDVI), and multi-domain exposome (socioeconomic, external environment, early-life environment, lifestyle-anthropometric)
limitations: INMA: relatively small sample size at each time-point, difficulty obtaining spirometry in young children, sample differences in sociodemographic characteristics, and no accounting for childhood phthalate exposure.
RHINESSA: low response rate (~40%) suggesting selection bias; highly correlated exposure windows and pollutants preventing multi-pollutant models.

NutriNet-Santé: health-conscious, better-educated participants limiting generalisability; missing exposures (aeroallergens, indoor dampness, built environment); non-binary asthma classification inducing potential classification bias.
